review_notes: Read the whole file and checked how the coordinate representative and l2Vec3Equiv definitions are used across the Leray directory. The file contains no @[simp] attributes, so I looked for missing canonical rewrite lemmas rather than conflicting or looping rules. I found two such gaps: there is no apply lemma for `realPartVectorL2Representative`, and none for `l2Vec3Equiv`. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested whether the proposed lemmas would work as simp rules. I did not report the private duplicates of `inner_l2BasisVec3` and `l2BasisVec3`, because that is duplication rather than a simp-interface problem.

findings.problem: The sibling definition `realVectorL2Representative` has a public evaluation lemma `realVectorL2Representative_apply`, which other files use to rewrite. `realPartVectorL2Representative` has no such lemma. The proofs of `realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal` and `realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae` therefore unfold the definition by name inside simp calls, together with `l2Vec3Equiv`. They also need an explicit `change` on a hypothesis to expose the coordinate form. The simp normal form is not pinned down, and the unfolding can expose the `ofLp`/`toLp` structure of `PiLp`.
findings.proposed_change: After the definition, add `theorem realPartVectorL2Representative_apply (v : ComplexVectorL2) (x : Vec3) : realPartVectorL2Representative v x = l2Vec3Equiv (realPartValue (v (WithLp.toLp 2 x))) := rfl`, or state the `ofLp` form that `realVectorL2Representative_apply` uses. Mark it `@[simp]` (or `@[simp, nolint simpNF]` if needed), and use it in place of the unfolding at lines 325 and 360. Together with the `l2Vec3Equiv` apply lemma below, this lets `simp` rewrite both representatives to coordinate form without unfolding the definitions.
findings.benefit: The real-part representative gets the same rewrite interface as the real one. Later proofs rewrite with one named lemma instead of unfolding the definition, and the `change ... at hp` workaround in the divergence-free proof becomes unnecessary.

findings.excerpt:
def l2Vec3Equiv : L2Vec3 ≃L[ℝ] Vec3 :=
  PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ)
findings.problem: `l2Vec3Equiv` is a public `@[expose]` definition with no simp lemma for application, for `l2Vec3Equiv x i`, or for its action on `l2BasisVec`. Every proof that needs its value passes the definition name to simp. Examples are `simp [l2BasisVec, l2Vec3Equiv, CKN.basisVec, Pi.single_apply]` and `simpa [F, realPartVectorL2Representative, l2Vec3Equiv] using hp`, and a similar call in `JSpaceFourierPotentialBase`. Unfolding drags in the `PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv` machinery, so each caller rediscovers the same normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem l2Vec3Equiv_apply (x : L2Vec3) : l2Vec3Equiv x = WithLp.ofLp x := rfl` or the `∀ i` coordinate form `l2Vec3Equiv x i = x i`. Mark it `@[simp]` after checking that it does not conflict with `PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv_apply`. Add `l2Vec3Equiv_l2BasisVec : l2Vec3Equiv (l2BasisVec i) = CKN.basisVec i`, the fact proved inline at lines 186–188. That fact is also closely related to the public `l2Vec3Equiv_symm_basisVec` in `JSpaceFourierPotentialBase`. Then drop `l2Vec3Equiv` from the simp sets.
findings.benefit: The definition no longer has to be unfolded by name. The inline `show ... by ext j; simp [...]` in `weakTestGradientSchwartz_apply` becomes a rewrite with a named lemma that other files can also use.
